entries.description: Project Rogue history and milestones in one scroll.
entries.fullText: project rogue codex project rogue timeline project rogue grows from the dransik/ashen empires lineage of 2d sandbox pvp. scroll through the years, from the early worlds to the game today. scroll to explore ↓ the line follows time, not a single chain of inheritance. each story identifies its relationship and links to its evidence. expand a card to read; open stories stay full size. 1999 official lineage dransik’s early worlds the original dransik takes shape, years before the classic name. read the story close story ⌄ asylumsoft’s archived news announces the worlds of dransik webpage on june 22, 1999, pre-alpha client 0.10 on july 9, and working player-versus-player melee on august 4. these are dated development milestones, rather than a definitive first launch date. a september 29 update describes isometric-engine work while the top-down game remains in use. a november announcement dates asylumsoft’s opening for business to october 28, 1999. the original game was called dransik. it later became known as dransik classic, continuing alongside the newer isometric game. sources asylumsoft · 1999 developer news, captured january 2000 link to this entry jun 12, 2002 official lineage dransik opens paid service youcangame opens paid accounts for the original dransik. read the story close story ⌄ following a june 6 distribution announcement, dransik’s june 12 news says youcangame is open and directs beta players to activate paid accounts. subsequent notices describe events and server updates. youcangame’s june faq lists subscriptions at $4.99 per month for existing beta players and $6.99 for new players, with a 14-day payment grace period. free testing continued separately. this commercial service preceded the newer isometric game’s march 2003 release. an october 2002 guide identifies youcangame’s paid server as the old-graphics version. sources dransik · june 12 opening notice, captured august 2002 youcangame · june 2002 subscription faq jeff barrett · october 2002 server notes link to this entry 2002 official lineage the dransik split classic and the newer isometric dransik coexist as distinct versions. read the story close story ⌄ jeff barrett’s october 2002 guide distinguishes an older-graphics youcangame server from the new isometric dransik new world beta. their quest and guild systems also differed. the guide lists new world, krythan inception in california, great wall in asia, and mystery and magic, an experimental magic-system server. these were server variants of the newer game—not four separate descendants. the newer branch is also referred to in historical accounts as new world / primordia / iso and later becomes ashen empires. sources jeff barrett · october 2002 server notes gamespot · january 2004 public beta link to this entry mar 2003 official lineage dransik 1.0 goes commercial the newer game launches commercially under the dransik name. read the story close story ⌄ the march 18 announcement calls the commercial release dransik 1.0 and describes a subscription service following its beta period. it separately mentions plans to re-release dransik classic. the original dransik already offered paid accounts in june 2002. this announcement concerns the newer game; its ashen empires identity follows in 2004. sources worthplaying · march 2003 announcement link to this entry jan 13, 2004 official lineage ashen empires public beta the newer dransik enters a public beta under its ashen empires identity. read the story close story ⌄ gamespot reports tko’s public beta announcement on january 13, 2004, explicitly identifying ashen empires as the game formerly known as dransik. tko describes phased development that lets existing subscribers continue playing while improvements are introduced. this is the newer/isometric product’s continuation, distinct from the classic branch. sources gamespot · january 2004 public beta link to this entry mar 8, 2004 official lineage classic goes offline tko discontinues dransik classic and invites its players to ashen empires. read the story close story ⌄ a march 8 press release, reproduced by mmorpg.com, announces the immediate discontinuation of dransik classic. players are invited to move to ashen empires. the separate shutdown is another reason to show classic and ashen empires as parallel product histories. sources mmorpg.com · classic discontinued link to this entry apr 2004 inspired descendant vorlia’s early alpha covad’s hobby project develops its own dransik-inspired world. read the story close story ⌄ a september 2004 archive preserves vorlia releases dated april 7 and april 11. alpha 0.0036 includes mining and guild functionality; 0.0037 adds pvp, guards, safe zones, smelting, and blacksmithing. the site describes a free hobby project seeking alpha testers. later releases add areas and equipment, dransik-style line of sight in october, and elemental damage and resistances in november. in january 2005, rheo joins to help with coding. the original credits identify covad as main coder, mdf as secondary coder, rheo as editor coder, devoc for design, and spide for graphics. jason ely / lothgar is thanked for dransik’s inspiration. arakard’s clarification, shared with the codex maintainer, states that the original vorlia/project rogue code does not overlap with dransik’s source and that their networking was substantially different. the april releases are documented milestones, not a confirmed first-ever launch. mdf’s expanded name remains unverified. sources vorlia · april–september 2004 alpha news vorlia · 2004–2005 release notes vorlia · february 2005 team credits arakard · original vorlia/project rogue source comparison, confirmed through the codex maintainer link to this entry 2005 creator successor lothgar online jason ely creates a temporary home for displaced dransik players. read the story close story ⌄ in his 2023 retrospective, ely dates lothgar online’s original launch to 2005 and describes it as a temporary sandbox while he developed new technology. it returned several times at community request. tristin later described joining ely’s lothgar team as a game designer after running the dransik online / inside ae fan site and developing empires online / one world. arakard recalls tristin as an early content developer while lothgar moved toward other projects. tristin’s precise employment dates and individual contributions remain undated here. sources ultima codex · ely’s september 2023 retrospective tristin · august 2017 development retrospective arakard · recollection shared with the codex maintainer link to this entry apr 5, 2006 official lineage dransik classic returns iron will games brings the original branch back online. read the story close story ⌄ mmorpg.com’s classic history dates its return to april 5, 2006, under iron will games. the revival continues the original classic line rather than creating another isometric dransik branch. sources mmorpg.com · classic history link to this entry 2005–2007 creator successor stygian worlds and early elderlands ely’s new technology has a name—and elderlands is already using its engine by 2007. read the story close story ⌄ an october 2005 community news reference associates jason ely with both lothgar online and stygian worlds. an april 2007 report then describes elderlands as a demo built with the stygian worlds core engine. this is a technology and creator relationship. the projects’ overlapping names and development do not establish a simple sequence of finished games replacing one another. sources dino’s ultima page · october 2005 neatorama · april 2007 report link to this entry 2008–2013 inspired descendant zonorian: the underground threat shel revives a dransik-inspired hobby mmorpg. read the story close story ⌄ a june 14, 2008 notice announces renewed development of zonorian, while saying the alpha is not yet ready for public testing. the notice survives in a 2012 capture. in an october 22, 2013 retrospective, shel explicitly names dransik as the inspiration and recalls making the first version roughly ten years earlier. he describes repeated restarts and offers account registration and downloads. the official credits identify dennis meelker, known as shel, as the developer, alongside contributors to graphics, story, and the website. the approximately 2003 beginning is a retrospective estimate, not a verified launch date. its reported influence on project rogue is recorded in the project rogue story. sources zonorian · june 2008 revival notice, captured august 2012 shel · october 2013 retrospective, captured december 2013 zonorian · december 2013 credits link to this entry 2012 related project a vorlia server closes a later vorlia operation redirects its community toward cyldan. read the story close story ⌄ the vorlia site at vorlia.arkku.net preserves a 2012 closure notice explaining that work is moving to a relaunched cyldan project. this documents one later vorlia operation, rather than the end of every project using the name. cyldan already had an archived website in 2006 and published team credits in 2007, including special thanks to jason ely. the exact source-code relationship between these projects is not established by the pages. the closure notice reads 03/04/2012; its day/month order is unresolved. sources vorlia · 2012 closure notice, captured april 2013 cyldan · february 2006 homepage cyldan · june 2007 credits link to this entry 2013 creator successor elderlands alpha milestone the existing codex records an alpha milestone, not the beginning of the engine. read the story close story ⌄ the earlier codex timeline places an elderlands alpha milestone in 2013. earlier reporting already names elderlands in 2007, so 2013 should not be presented as the origin of its technology. archive date: the 2013 alpha milestone is retained from the earlier codex; its exact timing still needs a contemporary launch source. sources previous codex history neatorama · april 2007 report link to this entry 2013–2014 inspired descendant noble’s land its creator describes a spiritual successor to dransik. read the story close story ⌄ an archived may–june 2013 development blog documents alpha work under dev mark and the besome games name. in a july 12, 2014 indiedb comment, the creator identifies himself as the dransik player noble and describes noble’s land as a spiritual successor, drawing on dransik and older ultima games. these are development records and the creator’s account of inspiration. the public sources reviewed here do not establish a vorlia source-code relationship or the game’s current operating status. sources noble’s land · may–june 2013 development blog noble · july 2014 creator comment link to this entry dec 18, 2016 source / engine vorlia source release vorlian posts a server, client, and tools release on ragezone. read the story close story ⌄ the dated release thread identifies vorlian as its author and advertises vorlia server, client, and tools. replies describe it as full source; a later reply reports that the download links no longer work. the release predates the codex’s july 2017 project rogue origin by about seven months. that chronology is relevant, but does not establish that this public upload was the source used by project rogue. sources ragezone · vorlia source release link to this entry feb–oct 2017 emulator / private server vorlian’s dransik / ae emulator public development threads document a separate isometric-game emulation effort. read the story close story ⌄ in february 2017, vorlian confirms ashen empires as the target of an old-mmo reverse-engineering project. a subsequent dransik server emu thread documents further development. keep this emulator branch separate from vorlia and project rogue: a shared community participant is not proof that the projects share an engine. sources ragezone · ashen empires reverse engineering ragezone · dransik server emu link to this entry jul 2017 community / engine lineage project rogue begins the codex records arakard and acry’s vorlia-based project rogue beginnings. read the story close story ⌄ the existing codex dates the project rogue / rogue online branch to july 2017 and credits arakard and acry with rebooting vorlia. its account describes revised stats, dransik-era systems, and pvp changes. according to arakard’s discord clarification, the original vorlia/project rogue codebase does not overlap with dransik’s source code. the connection to dransik is through inspiration and game systems, rather than shared source code. a community account relayed by the codex maintainer identifies zonorian as arakard’s main inspiration. zonorian’s own site documents its dransik influence; the specific features that influenced project rogue remain unrecorded here. this is a reported design influence, not evidence of shared code. the vorlia source release is a preceding milestone, not a proven delivery route. the exact source version and transfer history remain open research questions. archive account: the founder/date account comes from the existing codex. direct provenance for the source transfer has not been established here. sources community account · arakard’s zonorian inspiration, relayed by the codex maintainer. shel · zonorian’s dransik inspiration arakard · discord clarification shared with the codex maintainer; original vorlia/project rogue comparison confirmed. previous codex history ragezone · vorlia source release link to this entry aug 2017 community descendant eltaris: war for the lost kingdom tristin presents an intersect-based mmo concept. read the story close story ⌄ on august 6, 2017, tristin introduced eltaris, a proposed realm-versus-realm game with territorial control built using intersect. on august 22, he placed development on hold while awaiting source availability. its connection to this history is tristin’s earlier community and development work, including lothgar online. the thread documents a concept and development attempt, not a confirmed launch or inherited dransik/vorlia code. sources tristin · august 2017 eltaris development thread link to this entry dec 17, 2018 emulator / private server the emulator announces public opening vorlian announces public access after roughly two years of work. read the story close story ⌄ the dransik server emu thread describes upcoming closed testing in september 2018. on december 17, vorlian announces that the server will open publicly after two years of development. the later connection to dransik rebirth is plausible, but the accessible thread does not definitively identify the projects as the same server. probable relationship: emulator → dransik rebirth. the naming/identity link remains unconfirmed. sources ragezone · dransik server emu link to this entry may–sep 2019 emulator / private server dransik rebirth and its shutdown public coverage documents rebirth, followed by a disputed shutdown account. read the story close story ⌄ massivelyop covered dransik rebirth as an ashen empires rogue server in may 2019. in september, it reported that the server had gone offline following an operator-reported legal complaint. the publication added an update questioning that account. the alleged dmca / cease-and-desist explanation is therefore attributed to the operators, not presented as an independently settled legal finding. probable relationship to vorlian’s emulator; the shutdown explanation is disputed. sources massivelyop · may 2019 overview massivelyop · september 2019 report and update link to this entry may 2022 creator successor elderlands legacy and future the live 2016-era build and the refactored development branch receive separate names. read the story close story ⌄ asylumsoft’s announcement, reproduced by ultima codex, calls the live 2016 build elderlands legacy. elderlands future names the heavily refactored version under development. these are two branches within elderlands. the announcement describes plans at that time and does not establish that future later launched. sources ultima codex · legacy and future link to this entry dec 9, 2022 official lineage dransik 2.0 a rewritten client modernizes the continuing classic branch. read the story close story ⌄ iron will games’ launch announcement describes a completely rewritten client, modern ui controls, larger-monitor support, and windows / osx availability. this is modernization of dransik classic, not a newly discovered historical fork. further server modernization belongs to this continuing line; this entry anchors the verified client-launch milestone. sources iron will games · dransik 2.0 announcement steamdb · preserved launch announcement link to this entry sep 17, 2023 creator successor lothgar development ends ely ends further lothgar work and redirects attention toward elderlands. read the story close story ⌄ ultima codex’s september 18 report reproduces ely’s announcement from the previous day. he recounts multiple revivals and explains that they repeatedly diverted effort from elderlands. some newer lothgar gameplay systems were intended to move into elderlands. that is a stated development plan, not proof that every proposed transfer shipped. sources ultima codex · ely’s september 2023 announcement link to this entry oct 2023 creator successor elderlands team transition josh ely and a small team take on the project as jason’s employment changes. read the story close story ⌄ an october 31 report describes jason ely’s new employment limiting his ability to continue elderlands work and a handover to his son josh and a small team. this dated handover does not establish the state of development in 2026. current activity should be checked separately rather than labeling the game dead. sources ultima codex · josh ely takes over link to this entry feb 20, 2026 related project modern vorlia online a modern release carries the vorlia name; its original-source ancestry is unconfirmed. read the story close story ⌄ the official site advertises a february 20, 2026 launch and windows, linux, and android support. its linked google play listing shows an august 30, 2026 update, providing evidence of maintenance in 2026. the checked public pages do not establish whether this version uses covad’s original source. similar branding and genre do not settle its code ancestry. unconfirmed relationship: original vorlia → modern vorlia online. activity checked september 6, 2026. sources vorlia online · official launch notice google play · vorlia online link to this entry 2026 inspired descendant kisnard online continues an independently developed dransik classic-inspired mmo continues publishing updates. read the story close story ⌄ jay avondoglio’s official faq names dransik classic as the inspiration and describes a java client/server with mariadb. the official homepage carries release notes from 2026. kisnard belongs to the wider family through inspiration, rather than being labeled a dransik or vorlia source fork. this entry marks observed 2026 activity, not its original launch. sources kisnard online · developer faq kisnard online · release notes link to this entry 2017–today project rogue fresh wipes & live upkeep the community’s history continues through project rogue’s evolving world. read the story close story ⌄ the codex’s ongoing project rogue account describes wipes, balance changes, and content updates. this is the continuation of the project rogue branch, not evidence that all neighboring projects merged into it. the archive preserves the older worlds and experiments as related histories, with uncertain connections kept explicit. sources previous codex history link to this entry related branches & open questions related projects whose dates, scope, or connections remain partly unresolved. unresolved connection lorvia and cyldan a 2006 notice links the lothgar online and vorlia names. read the story close story ⌄ a cyldan homepage captured on february 5, 2006 announces cancellation and directs readers toward “lorvia (lothgar online + vorlia = lorvia).” the page also retains a release countdown, leaving its precise sequence of updates unclear. this is a contemporary reference to a connection, but it does not name the people involved in an agreement or document a completed joint release. vorlia’s 2004–2005 credits list covad and other contributors, with lothgar thanked for inspiration. a later site at lorvia.net describes an offline rpg becoming lorvia online. the inspected page does not identify covad, lothgar, or vorlia, so the matching name alone does not establish that it is the same project. sources cyldan · february 2006 lorvia notice vorlia · february 2005 credits lorvia.net · july 2007 capture; identity unresolved link to this entry reported engine experiment arakard’s dransik-on-vorlia experiment a supplied community post reports classic content running on the vorlia engine. read the story close story ⌄ the supplied lothgar online facebook post reportedly says arakard had dransik classic running using the vorlia engine. it could help explain the technical context around project rogue. arakard separately clarifies that the original vorlia/project rogue codebase does not overlap with dransik’s source, whose networking was substantially different. the reported experiment should therefore not be read as evidence that dransik source code was incorporated into vorlia or project rogue. this clarification does not independently verify the experiment’s details or date. the post could not be independently retrieved during this review. its date and wording remain unverified here; it is preserved as a research lead, not used to prove a source transfer or a direct causal link. unconfirmed source check: historical breadcrumb supplied by the research pack. sources arakard · discord clarification shared with the codex maintainer; original vorlia/project rogue comparison confirmed. lothgar online · supplied historical post link to this entry vorlia clone luxtrin the project’s own site explicitly identifies it as a vorlia clone. read the story close story ⌄ luxtrin’s official page describes a work-in-progress clone of vorlia and credits covad with vorlia. it directs visitors to discord for an alpha client. the self-described relationship is established. the page’s 2022 copyright footer is not a reliable launch date, and its availability alone does not prove active development in 2026. sources luxtrin · official project description link to this entry community descendant empires online → one world a dransik fan-site community moves into an independently built game. read the story close story ⌄ in a first-person retrospective, tristin describes running dransik online / inside ae, building empires online and later one world with players from that community, and moving from player worlds / mirage to fso. he also describes later joining jason ely’s lothgar team as a game designer. this establishes a reported community and personnel connection, not inheritance of dransik source code. precise project dates remain unresolved. sources tristin · first-person development history link to this entry

entries.fullText: floor cleanup system creeper the creeper is the automated sweep that removes abandoned loot from the floor. cycle 3 minutes cleanup runs on a recurring 3 minutes sweep interval. threshold more than 8 minutes ground items are removed when their undisturbed time is more than 8 minutes during a sweep. lifetime 8-11 minutes untouched loot normally remains on the floor for 8-11 minutes, with best-case timing up to 11 minutes. sweep timing preview cleanup runs every 3 minutes. just before 8m just after sweep typical window selected case worst case item survives about 8 minutes. item reaches 8 minutes just before a sweep, then is eligible when that sweep checks it.

entries.title: Encounter
entries.description: Encounter flow, spawns, and tuning knobs.
entries.fullText: encounter control spawn source open-world monster spawns flow through pre-authored encounter nodes. layout chunk painting each encounter paints a monster layout chunk-by-chunk across the map. sets 5 weighted groups encounters can define up to five weighted monster sets with per-monster quantity ranges. tuning respawn & radius spawn radius, respawn cadence, active state, and despawn rules shape the pressure. active vs passive active state 10 chunks (160 tiles) the encounter is active while a player is within range of its center. most encounters increase their spawn rate while active. going active after 4+ minutes passive triggers a just activated spawn pulse. passive state out of range if no player is in range, the encounter remains passive. leaving range starts the elite grace countdown when the encounter had prolonged activity. re-entering the 10-chunk radius during grace refreshes the timer. escalation flow 1 enter range a player moves within 10 chunks, making the encounter active. 2 hold pressure after 1 minute of continuous active time , the encounter gains prolonged activity. 3 unlock variants prolonged activity allows elite, corrupted, and elite+ monsters to spawn. 4 leave or refresh the encounter keeps eligibility through a 6-minute grace window after going passive. variant rules elite purple lightning spawn chance: 1 in 33 3x health and 1.5x damage 3x drop rate base rarity: rare corrupted green lightning spawn chance: 1 in 66 spawn time: night only 5x health and 1.75x damage 5x drop rate and corrupts loot base rarity: rare elite+ yellow lightning spawn chance: 1 in 100 10x health and 2x damage 10x drop rate base rarity: epic despawns and leashes inactivity 4-minute rule monsters despawn after four continuous minutes without moving or attacking. uptime 1-hour cap any monster exceeding one hour of uptime despawns regardless of activity. exceptions spires demon spires, dragon spires, and master spires ignore the 4-minute inactivity rule. bosses locale leash dragging a boss outside its locale forces an instant leash, reset, and full health restore.

entries.title: Corruption System
entries.description: How corruption overrides innates, drop sources, and cleansing.
entries.fullText: corruption override corrupted innate corruption replaces the item's normal innate perk line with its corrupted perk line. sources hard bosses corrupted loot is tied to hard boss and corrupted-monster sources; item pages are the place to confirm exact drops. cleanse purge tool plan check gear pages weapon and armor detail panels show both normal perks and corrupted perk values when the data has them. what corruption changes corrupted item innate line changes the item keeps its identity, slot, rarity state, base requirements, and normal stat ranges. the normal innate perk is overridden by the item's corrupted perk. some items use a specific alternate perk rather than a simple tier increase. cleaned item normal innate returns cleanse targets the corrupted innate, not an applied imbuement or special effect. after cleansing, evaluate the item by its normal innate and remaining gear values. use purge for cleanup; use reforge or ascend for item improvement decisions. example dark sword epidemic t3 -> crimson feast t1 use the item detail view to compare the innate perk against the corrupted perk line.

entries.title: Anti-Zerg
entries.fullText: anti-zerg purpose smaller squad cushion targets of pvp damage receive reduction when their guild size is smaller than the attacker's side. modes warfront & open-world the system runs in warfront zones and open-world range/hash checks. penalty self-heal mirror the same percentage is applied as a penalty to offensive self-healing against protected targets. cap 30% maximum published reduction ranges cap at 30% for the smaller qualifying squad. damage reduction calculator only the smaller squad can receive reduction. my guild — 3 players enemy guild — 8 players damage reduction 30% my guild is smaller (3 players); enemy guild is larger (8 players) my guild receives the max 30% damage reduction. mode and sizing rules open-world mode 3-minute high-water zerg size is the highest guild count in your area over the last 3 minutes . the world is split into 128x128 tiles hashes, or 8x8 chunks. range-based sizing groups guildmates within 10 chunks (160 tiles) . guildmates in your hash or immediately surrounding hashes count toward your zerg. underground hashes are calculated with the hashes directly above them. warfront mode bundled zones a warfront bundles marked pvp areas into one anti-zerg zone. while inside, every guildmate in the warfront counts toward your zerg size. leaving the warfront boundary switches sizing back to range-based mode. qualifying links persist for 180 seconds , even if spacing changes. focus fire and collaboration 1 become active after 10+ direct attacks in 10 minutes , your guild is an active pvp participant. 2 pick a focus target if over 66% of your guild's damage hits one guild, that guild becomes your focus target. 3 combine collaborators multiple guilds focusing the same target are collaborators and their anti-zerg values entries.title: Monster Damage Reduction
entries.description: How monster damage reduction scales and affects combat.
entries.fullText: monster damage reduction start threshold +20 level gap no monster scaling applies until the monster is more than 20 levels above you. full effect +30 level gap at +30 or higher, the monster scaling is fully capped. max shift 25% monsters can deal up to 25% more damage and take up to 25% less damage. level 100 cap monsters 100+ for this calculation, monsters 100+ count as 100 before the level gap is checked. damage reduction calculator monster levels above 100 are treated as 100. player level 25 monster level 50 level difference +25 5 levels into the +20 to +30 window. scaling amount 12.5% applied to both monster damage boost and their damage reduction. monster damage dealt 112.5% damage you receive after the monster's bonus. your damage vs monster 87.5% your outgoing damage after the monster's reduction. at +25, monsters deal 12.5% more damage and take 12.5% less from you. threshold reference +20 or less 0% no monster bonus and no reduction against your damage. +25 12.5% monster damage dealt is 112.5%; your damage vs monster is 87.5%. +30 or more 25% monster damage dealt is 125%; your damage vs monster is 75%. level 100 cap 100 monsters above level 100 use treated level 100 for this calculation.

entries.title: PVP System
entries.fullText: pvp world open combat players can fight anywhere outside protected towns and marked safe areas. safe zone safe zone dove safe zones show a dove icon on the bottom-right hud so risk state is readable in-game. death backpack + gear death returns you to your marked spawn, drops your backpack, and normally drops one equipped item. decay body timers bodies become lootable after 4 minutes and fully drop after 10 minutes . safe zones and flagging protected areas read the hud town safety is communicated by the dove icon. outside safe zones, pvp is open-world and lethal. safe-zone status matters before duels, escorts, and gear swaps. criminal status grey name flag attacking any player or npc turns your name grey. status clears after 5 minutes out of sight of players and npcs. temporary criminals can be killed or looted without adding offense counts. death and loot flow 1 death resolves you respawn at your marked spawn, or at the nearest criminal gate if you died criminal. 2 gear drops your backpack drops, plus one equipped item in normal death rules. 3 looted item flag items taken from the body at 4 minutes are flagged looted and drop on every death. 4 clean ground drop if untouched until 10 minutes , the body drops items clean with no carried loot flag. criminal consequences kills 2 counts the last hit on a kill grants two offense counts. looting 1 count looting a non-criminal item adds one offense count. guards 50+ counts guards jail you once you reach 50 counts. active crim execute on sight if your criminal status is still active, guards execute you instead of dragging you to jail. sentence work counts down wait it out, or smash rocks and dump them in the crusher to reduce offense counts. set gear set weapon check if a weapon only works with a full armor set, losing any set piece makes that weapon drop too. tracking and community project rogue feeds global-chat mirrors in-game global chat live into discord. project rogue feeds kill-feed posts kills, sprees, and kill/assist ratios for killer and victim. daily boards leaderboard-levels top 20 level ladder updated every 24 hours. daily boards leaderboard-kills top 40 kill ladder updated every 24 hours. daily boards leaderboard-shards top 40 shard ladder updated every 24 hours.

entries.title: Guild
entries.fullText: guild hotkey press g opens the guild panel so you can inspect identity, roster, rank, and management controls. roster cap 50 members the panel shows the active member count as ## / 50 . ranks member to leader guild roles display as member, elder, council, or leader. parties party a/b/c the guild party control cycles selected members through party a, party b, and party c. identity and roster clan identity name and tag the clan name and tag identify the guild. the tag appears in front of your character name in-game. roster rows [rank] character name each roster line shows the member rank beside the character name in a scrollable list. leader leader name the panel lists the current leader separately so ownership is easy to confirm. capacity ## / 50 use the member count to understand whether the guild has room for another invite. operations reference invite add member add a player to the guild when the roster has open capacity. remove kick member remove the selected member from the guild roster. rank up promote raise the selected member's rank. rank down demote lower the selected member's rank. party guild party cycles selected members through party a, party b, and party c. exit leave leave the current guild. pvp and group context anti-zerg sizing guild counts matter anti-zerg compares guild participation during pvp. party a/b/c helps organize players, while the anti-zerg page covers the actual combat sizing rules. communication guild chat guild chat messages are visible only to members of your guild.

entries.title: Experience Pool
entries.description: Experience pool behavior and XP flow.
entries.fullText: experience pool pool cap 3.0 levels the pool caps at 3.0 levels for every character. bonus double xp stored pool doubles xp earned from hunting while pool remains. drain 1% = 0.01 pool each 1% of a level gained consumes 0.01 pool; a 25% level gain costs 0.25 pool. empty normal xp when the pool is empty, xp returns to the normal rate until the pool refills. daily pool build levels 1-89 +3.0 levels per 24 hours characters below level 90 rebuild the pool at the full daily rate. levels 90+ +1.0 level per 24 hours high-level characters rebuild more slowly, while the cap remains 3.0 levels. at cap paused passive gain pauses at 3.0 levels until you spend pool through combat xp.

entries.title: Deconstruct
entries.fullText: deconstruct currency shard conversion deconstruct turns gear into ascendency shards ; higher rarity and level grant more shards. value inspect payout select an eligible backpack item to see its shard payout before confirming. weapon and armor details also list deconstruction and promotion values. dirty loot half value deconstructing dirty looted items returns half the normal shard value. imbuements t1 returns deconstructing t1 imbuements from the craft menu returns 25 tattered imbuements . finality no takebacks every deconstruct is final; shards go to your inventory and the original item cannot be recovered. how to deconstruct 1 open deconstruct press [r] , then open the deconstruct tab. 2 inspect payout select a backpack item to preview its shard return. 3 single item click select , then decon . 4 deconstruct all three presses, then a fourth click to confirm. includes every eligible backpack item. deconstruction is permanent. check your backpack before using deconstruct all.

entries.title: Ascend
entries.description: Ascend process and ascendant gear basics.
entries.fullText: ascend currency ascendency shards ascend spends the shards generated by deconstructing unwanted gear. item ceiling max rarity every item has a maximum rarity tier. capped items cannot be promoted further. upgrade step one tier each successful ascend raises the item's current rarity by one tier. cost preview promotion cost weapon and armor detail pages expose each item's promotion value. menu backpack items the ascend menu lists eligible backpack items with costs, stat totals, and current rolls. what changes changes current rarity rises one tier. stat ranges, armor bonuses, and perk eligibility follow the new rarity. what stays fixed item identity, max rarity , base values, and drop or craft sources. in ascend, select a backpack item, review its promotion cost, and confirm the upgrade.

entries.title: Imbuements
entries.fullText: imbuements material tattered imbuement each tatter is tied to one perk name. matching tatters are the material used to craft that perk scroll. craft 250 matching tatters spend 250 matching tatters in the craft menu to create one scroll of imbuement. apply epic+ item use the imbuement tool to apply a crafted scroll of imbuement to an epic+ weapon or armor piece. recover 25 tattered imbuements purging or converting a t1 imbuement returns 25 tattered imbuements of that perk type. imbue collect matching tatters → craft a scroll of imbuement → apply with the imbue tool. three-copy perk cap, including race bonuses. tatter drops uncommon tatter roughly 1 in 10 eligible triggers. rare tatter roughly 1 in 20 eligible triggers. level scaling quantity: 2 to max(3, level / 10) . tier roll odds the perk is fixed; the tier rolls when applied. 80% t1 15% t2 5% t3 example sources hell spawn bloodthirster / bloodlust werewolf juggernaut / parry bloodthirster perk details & sources

entries.title: Reforge
entries.description: Reforge Epic-or-higher equipment using rarity shards.
entries.fullText: reforge eligibility epic+ the current client describes reforge as an action for epic-or-higher equipment. currency rarity shards rare, epic, mythical, and ascendant reroll shards form the current shard family. menu tinker tools open tinker tools, choose reforge, then select the equipment you want to reforge. outcome fresh stat spread stats are rerolled within the item's current rarity tier. what changes changes a new strength, dexterity, and constitution spread. total stats can vary within the current rarity range. what does not change item identity, current rarity , max rarity , base values, and sources. reforging replaces the current stat roll; a better result is not guaranteed.

entries.title: Purge
entries.description: Purge or cleanse items and recover Tattered Imbuements.
entries.fullText: purge purge or cleanse purge removes an applied special effect or imbuement. returns 25 tattered imbuements of that effect type. cleanse removes the corrupted innate from corrupted gear, restoring its normal innate. recovery rules no tier refund the original scroll and tier roll are not returned. no item reset rarity, base stats, and the item ceiling stay unchanged. epic+ item required to apply a replacement imbuement. the removed effect is lost. purge returns 25 tatters, not the original 250-tatter craft cost.
